pravartante ca yāgāni tāni te kathayāmyaham || 3 ||

yatra rājanti [rajyanti iti syāt kim] vai gāvastathā'nye mṛgajātayaḥ || 14 ||

śubhe vāre'nukūle'tha digvidik siddhimācaret [k, g: siddhamācaret] ||

translation: Then, O lotus-born one, he should instruct the disciple who has arrived.

sanskrit: yattadājñāpayet [k: yasta] taṃ vai gaccha putra dhanaṃ yataḥ || 2 ||
translation: Whatever he commands — go there, indeed, O son, whence the wealth (comes).

sanskrit: yathālabdhaṃ tu tat paścādgurave vinivedya ca || 3 ||
translation: And having afterwards announced to the guru whatever was obtained...

sanskrit: dayāṃ kuru tvanāthasya [kh: kuruṣvānāthasya] nimagnasya bhavārṇave || 4 ||
translation: Show compassion to the helpless one sunk in the ocean of existence.
For that purpose, the guru should undertake the worship of the maṇḍala.

sanskrit: likhitvā kuṅkumādyairvā cālikhya [k, g: vālikhya] ghaṭikādikaiḥ [kh: -kādibhiḥ] || 6 ||
translation: Having written, or having drawn with saffron and the like, with ghaṭikās and so forth...
He should worship with fruits, flowers and so on — wild (plants) that are always available [kh: water-born ones].

sanskrit: ādyaṃpadmodarākhyaṃ [kh: padmodbhavākhyaṃ] tu na [k, kh: tatvasaṃkhyopa] tu saṃkhyopalakṣitam || 8 ||
translation: The first is called 'Lotus-belly' (padmodara); but it is not characterized by number [k, kh: characterized by the tattva-count].
And that lotus-circle is of many kinds; the third (kind is)...

sanskrit: miśracakrābhidhānaṃ tu maṇḍalaṃ bahu bhedayuk [kh: - bhedadhṛk] || 10 ||
translation: But the maṇḍala called 'Miśracakra' (the Mixed Circle) is endowed with many divisions.

sanskrit: mahākhyaṃ navanābhaṃ tu bimbabhedena yat sthitam [kh: smṛtam] || 11 ||
translation: The one called 'Great' is nine-naved, which stands [kh: is known] by distinction of form.

sanskrit: mokṣo yena bhavatyāśu bhaktānāṃ kevalena ca || 12 ||
translation: By which liberation quickly comes to devotees, and by it alone.

sanskrit: dvādaśyāṃ pratipakṣaṃ tu vatsarānte tato dvijam || 13 ||
translation: On the twelfth (of each) fortnight, and at the year's end, then the twice-born...
For by (the Lord) seen, even worshipped, and meditated upon in the heart, indeed...
And moreover at the beginning, then at the completion, (it) is to be worshipped with devotion.
Then, upon that offense (?), his two (things) proceed — even the remnants...

sanskrit: tṛtīyamaṇḍale ceṣṭvā tatra taṃ ca praveśayet || 18 ||
translation: And having worshipped in the third maṇḍala, he should lead him in there.
And by a triad of fortnights deficient by five days...
The fruits of that arise for him in due sequence, O twice-born.
The fourth is the great yāga, by which he would attain the status of ācārya.

sanskrit: dvija śeṣadinānāṃ tu hyekaikaṃ tu samāpayet || 22 ||
translation: O twice-born, of the remaining days he should complete each one (individually).
He reaches the far shore of the ocean of saṃsāra, hard to cross, O Brahman.
In this wilderness of saṃsāra the lamps of knowledge have been made by you (?)...

sanskrit: nityaṃ viprāstikānāṃ ca śraddhā saṃyamasevinām [k, g: saṃyami] || 25 ||
translation: And faith (arises) always in believing Brahmins who practice restraint.
Having embarked on the boat of the yāga, (the goal) is to be known as characterized by the far shore.

sanskrit: kṛpayā parayā'viṣṭo yo vidvān sa gurussmṛtaḥ || 27 ||
translation: Whoever is a learned one possessed of supreme compassion, he is known as a guru.
He who rescues (the disciple) by the hand of the yāga — that guru is known as my equal.
Of those worshipped and honored with flowers, garments, and ornaments...
While oblations are being offered into the fire with the sounds of Vedic chanting...
For (it is) always (to be kept) from haters, those of corrupted reasoning, and atheists.
And evil disposition and evil reasoning — atheism would go to dissolution.
By his power — how much more so in those beginning with faith!
Absorbed in that, always engaged, his mind free of vikalpa (mental constructs).
Whether a celibate student or a householder, (he is) one whose task is accomplished, according to rule.
Wise, clear-minded, well-content, longing for the vision of the truth (tattva).
Having obtained the qualified vessel (pātra) and completed the yāga-initiation...
The past, present, and future, O lotus-born one.
And (it is) to be spoken together with the pervasion of the tattvas, as it stands.
Appearing as everything yet non-appearing, characterized by consciousness, being, and bliss.
By that this is manifested; standing in which (state) one would attain sameness (with it).
(It is) to be done by you, always, necessarily, for those afraid of the terrors of saṃsāra.
And having made the self-knowledge abide in the pātra, he should cast off the body (piṇḍa).
The supreme, purifying knowledge that dispels the darkness of ignorance.
Of the timid and the unawakened, of the conquered — (in) the unsteady (?)...
And of those whose rites are incomplete, of those who have obtained knowledge from you, O Lord...
O dear one, from the fulfillment of the rites — the intention of the unaccomplished one, and...
And the boundless ocean of existence — (crossing it) without weariness (?) — the supreme abode.
And the accomplished, and the one being accomplished, and the third — the one who wishes to ascend.
Just as one remains satisfied, having eaten before, his meal (already) secured...
At the conclusions (of the rites), for all of them, non-satisfaction is not reckoned a fault.

sanskrit: kālena svamate [svamateśasti dve] śāsta  ? dve tasminnavyaye pade || 52 ||
translation: In time, according to one's own view — two (readings?) ... two, in that imperishable abode.

sanskrit: saṃsārottārakaśśaśvadyayā vai [k, g: vai tatavadvijaḥ] tattvaviddvijaḥ || 53 ||
translation: The rescuer from saṃsāra — always, by which, indeed — the twice-born who knows the tattva.
From the presence of those established in radiant samādhi, (beginning) with birth, together with...
The first chapter (colophon).

sanskrit: eṣāmuktastvanantastu pravāsaṃ  ? ca svayaṃ ca yaḥ || 1 ||
translation: Of these the endless one has been spoken; (he) who himself (undertakes) the sojourn, and...
There are places of many kinds there, O lotus-born one.

sanskrit: pravartante ca yāgāni tāni te kathayāmyaham || 3 ||
translation: And the yāgas take place there; those I will relate to you.
In a delightful forest on the ground (?), crowded with trees and herbs...

sanskrit: kūleṣu nimnagānāṃ tu tāsāmapi ca saṅgame || 5 ||
translation: On the banks of rivers, and at the confluence of those (rivers) too...
In the precinct of a deity's temple, in cow-pens, in a Brahmin hermitage...

sanskrit: tatra bhūmiṃ parīkṣyādau lakṣaṇāḍhyāṃ [ga - lakṣaṇārthāṃ] sulakṣitāam [kh: surakṣitām] || 7 ||
translation: There, having first examined the ground — rich in (auspicious) marks, well-marked [kh: well-protected]...
For the purpose of performing the yāgas, and for the purpose of a house for householders...
There are (these kinds) of ground, in brief; listen to me as I state it.
But that ground is faulty; it would produce many obstacles.
Which is furnished with tranquil trees, crowded with fruits and flowers...
Pleasant to the touch, with smooth waters, rich in fragrance, sweet and dark...
Free from foul smells and other great faults, bestowing happiness and peace.

sanskrit: yatra rājanti [rajyanti iti syāt kim] vai gāvastathā'nye mṛgajātayaḥ || 14 ||
translation: Where cows shine [or: 'rajyanti' — if that should be (the reading)] and likewise other kinds of deer...
The sight (of it) produces delight quickly, as if among one's own beloveds.
Crowded with kumuda, utpala, and kahlāra lotuses, with sārasa cranes and so on...
A great arrow-reed grove on the left is recommended; on the right, a tree (or hill).
For which (site) tanks, wells, and the like are dug in the northeast and on the north...
In the hot season (its touch is) like the moon's cool rays — such is the blessed ground.
The sound of bronze vessels, bells, the strains of lute and flute — auspicious.

sanskrit: samārdhaṃ vā samaṃ khātvā pāṃsumuddhṛtya pūrayet || 21 ||
translation: Having dug to half or full depth, having removed the loose earth, he should fill (it in).
Know (it as) incomplete, lowest; being faulty, one should abandon it.

sanskrit: pradhānā madhyamā nyūnā sā mahī parikīrtitā || 23 ||
translation: That ground is proclaimed best, middling, or deficient (according to its qualities).
Raised like a tortoise's back, suitable, very auspicious, with a surface like a mirror...
And the ground shaped like a garland or a crown — effecting all accomplishments.
Because it causes the loss of siddhis, it is to be avoided from afar.
Having taken (the ground) as common to all, having worshipped the mantras, with them he should perform the worship...
Having anointed (?) with much ghee in the middle region, as (it is) situated...

sanskrit: tyaktvā tu dviguṇātmānaṃ bhāyāmidhmani [kh: chāyā] garbhavat || 29 ||
translation: But having abandoned the double(-length shadow) ... (in) the fuel (?) — [kh: shadow] like a fetus...
With meat (obtained) without violence, with parched grain, with water...
Boiled, blended together with curds, milk, and jaggery...

sanskrit: digvidikṣu tathā madhye tvidamuktvā baliṃ kṣipet || 32 ||
translation: In the directions and intermediate directions, likewise in the middle — having said this, he should cast the bali-offering.

sanskrit: te prayacchantu me tuṣṭiṃ prayāntu paramālayam || 33 ||
translation: Let them give me satisfaction; let them go to the supreme abode.
He should command the beings; afterwards he should dig the ground up to the water (?).
Having summoned (them) in the very pure (waters?), fragrance-rich, indeed unmixed (?)...
Afterwards, (the ground) filled with rice, with even grasses and tree-shoots...
Having purified (it) on the fourth day, (the ground) turned over with ploughs...

sanskrit: tataḥ kāñcanajaṃ reṇuṃ * * * * jaṃ [k: tāmratāmurayapi; g - tāmratāyurayaṃcapi] tārajaṃ tathā || 38 ||
translation: Then gold-produced dust, ...-produced [lacuna; k: copper...; g: copper...], and likewise silver-produced...
Rich with flowers, unbroken grains, and parched rice, and mixed with white mustard and sesame seeds.

sanskrit: akṛte vā kṛte khāte śuddhimeti ca tatkṣaṇāt || 40 ||
translation: Whether the digging is done or not done, it attains purification immediately.
For purification, for auspiciousness, and indeed for the purification of the site...
Then, having leveled (the ground), when ... would be before the flood (?)...
Again, (it is) to be pressed with broad pestles made of sacrifice-wood (?).
Having smeared and wiped (it) clean, then with the hand or with a garment...

sanskrit: śubhe vāre'nukūle'tha digvidik siddhimācaret [k, g: siddhamācaret] ||
translation: On an auspicious, favorable day, then, in the directions and intermediate directions, he should undertake the siddhi(-rite).
The second chapter (colophon).
